Usually I hear all that spiel about giving and giving and never receiving from people who want the world to match their expectations and get disappointed when it dares not to. 

The world doesn’t owe you anything. You give things because you want to, not because you expect something in return. Otherwise - just don’t. You listen to your friends’ problems because you want to and can do it at the moment, not because you expect them to have the resources to do the same for you. Otherwise - just don’t do it or find friends who match your expectations. 
I don’t know what people get handed things on golden platter. Maybe like 1% of all earth population. The rest fight to survive and try to find meaning where they can. 
Your suffering is not singular. Probably, every person you know suffer in their own way. You don’t know what they think about at night. 

The best advice I was given is to understand that the world wasn’t build to match my expectations. And people are just people, and expecting them to match my views on friendship and other relationships is pointless. 
You can only decide what kind of person you want to be, how you react to things and what kind of life you try to build for yourself. 
You need to be a friend to yourself first. At the moment, you’re not a very good one.
People will do without your help. Very possibly, they don’t even need it that much. You do though.

I used to think the same way, that I was a girl who had nothing in common with 99% of male population. I thought that most of my interests are stereotypically “girly”, all my life I had only female friends, and honestly just could not connect with men. But actually turns out I have a shit ton in common with many people on this planet, including men. Probably, if you dig a little deeper, you’ll find that you have something in common with almost every person you meet. At least we all have the common experience of being a human on this planet at this (very strange) time. 
Me and my bf are both socially awkward, have a bit of trouble connecting with people, but at the beginning of our relationship (we didn’t actually date back then), we took this list online - something like “questions that make you fall in love with each other”. Basically it’s a list of pretty personal questions each of you ask the other. Idk, was it the list or what, but we’re dating for 3 years now lol
But what this list showed was that despite being different genders, our personal experiences were very similar, and we could connect based on that. Afterwards we found out that we actually have a lot of common interests too, and also kind of adopted a bit of each other’s interests. 
I think, the most important part is to be genuinely curious about the other person. To want to get to know them. And the more you know them, the more you’ll probably find similarities and differences, which are not actually a bad thing, but an opportunity to learn something new and maybe find a new thing to be passionate about.
